description: Engineering software that works, scales and can be maintained: processes, requirements, modelling, architecture and design, user interfaces, verification, testing, maintenance and the management of teams, all exercised in a term-long team project. Taught to the depth of a leading software engineering course.
modelledOn: Pressman and Maxim, Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach
Fox and Patterson, Engineering Software as a Service: An Agile Approach Using Cloud Computing
IEEE SWEBOK Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge
outcomes: Compare software process models and choose and tailor one for a given project.
Elicit, specify, validate and manage requirements with user stories and formal specifications.
Model systems with UML and design them with sound architecture and design principles and patterns.
Design user interfaces that follow established principles and are evaluated with users.
Verify and validate software with reviews, static analysis and tests at unit, integration and system level.
Plan maintenance and evolution and manage a software team with agile practices and measurable progress.

units.title: Software engineering and process models
topics: What software engineering is; the cost of failure (Therac-25, Ariane 5, local e-government projects)
Software processes: waterfall, incremental, spiral, RUP; agile methods: XP, Scrum, Kanban; DevOps
Process activities: specification, development, validation, evolution
Choosing and tailoring a process; process improvement and CMMI in brief
Project team formation and tooling: Git, issue tracker, CI

units.title: Software requirements
topics: Functional and non-functional requirements; quality attributes
Elicitation: interviews, observation, workshops, prototypes, scenarios; stakeholders
User stories, acceptance criteria, use cases; the software requirements specification
Requirements validation, prioritisation (MoSCoW), traceability and change management
Formal specification in brief: pre- and post-conditions, invariants

units.title: System models with UML
topics: Context, interaction, structural and behavioural models
Use case, activity, sequence, class, state machine, component and deployment diagrams
Model-driven engineering in brief; keeping models and code consistent
Modelling the team project

units.title: Architectural design
topics: Architecture and its influence on quality attributes; architectural views
Patterns: layered, client-server, MVC, pipe-and-filter, repository, microservices, event-driven
Application architectures: transaction processing, information systems, language processing
Documenting architecture; architectural decision records

units.title: Design and implementation
topics: Object-oriented design process; design principles: SOLID, cohesion and coupling, information hiding
Design patterns: Observer, Strategy, Factory, Adapter, Facade, Command, Singleton and when not to use them
Implementation issues: reuse, configuration management, host-target development, open source and licensing
Code quality: style, reviews, refactoring, technical debt, static analysis
APIs, interfaces and contracts; defensive programming and error handling

units.title: User interface design principles
topics: User-centred design; usability principles and heuristics; consistency, feedback, error recovery
Interaction styles; information presentation; colour and accessibility
Prototyping and evaluating the team project's interface with users
Internationalisation and designing for low-end devices

units.title: Verification and validation
topics: Verification versus validation; the V-model; inspections and reviews
Static analysis, linters, type checkers, model checking in brief
Test planning; test-driven development; code coverage and its limits
Formal methods and when they are worth it; safety-critical systems

units.title: Software testing
topics: Unit testing with a framework; mocks and stubs; property-based testing
Black-box techniques: equivalence partitioning, boundary values, decision tables; white-box: statement, branch, path coverage
Integration, system, acceptance, regression, performance, security and usability testing
Test automation in CI; test documentation and defect tracking

units.title: Software maintenance and evolution
topics: Lehman's laws; types of maintenance; the cost of change
Legacy systems: assessment, reengineering, migration, strangler pattern
Refactoring, continuous evolution, release management and versioning
Software metrics for maintainability and quality

units.title: Project and team management
topics: Risk management, estimation (story points, COCOMO in brief), scheduling, tracking velocity and burndown
Teamwork: roles, communication, motivation, conflict; distributed and remote teams
Quality management and standards (ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 25010); configuration management
Professional ethics and the ACM/IEEE code; project presentation and retrospective
